units.inflation: percentage points at an annual rate (4 x the quarterly rate)
units.policy_rate: percentage points at an annual rate, deviation from steady state

calibration.source: Galí (2015), ch. 3, pp. 67-70 (checked against J. Pfeifer's Dynare replication Gali_2015_chapter_3.mod)

sources.beta: Galí (2015), ch. 3, pp. 67-70 (checked against J. Pfeifer's Dynare replication Gali_2015_chapter_3.mod)
sources.sigma: Galí (2015), ch. 3, pp. 67-70 (checked against J. Pfeifer's Dynare replication Gali_2015_chapter_3.mod)
sources.kappa: Galí (2015), ch. 3, pp. 67-70 (checked against J. Pfeifer's Dynare replication Gali_2015_chapter_3.mod): kappa from beta, sigma, phi, alpha, epsilon, theta
sources.phi_pi: Galí (2015), ch. 3, pp. 67-70 (checked against J. Pfeifer's Dynare replication Gali_2015_chapter_3.mod)
sources.phi_y: Galí (2015), ch. 3, pp. 67-70 (checked against J. Pfeifer's Dynare replication Gali_2015_chapter_3.mod) (0.5/4 at quarterly rates); Galí's rule responds to output's deviation from steady state; here no shock moves natural output, so that equals the output gap
sources.rho_demand: Galí (2015), ch. 3, pp. 67-70 (checked against J. Pfeifer's Dynare replication Gali_2015_chapter_3.mod) (discount-rate shock)
sources.rho_cost_push: our choice, set equal to rho_demand; the model has no cost-push shock in that chapter

demand_shock.label: spending shock (households less patient)
demand_shock.shock: households become less patient (Galí's discount-rate shock), a demand shift: the natural rate of interest rises 1 percentage point a year on impact
demand_shock.committee_note: the committee's scientific background (p. 29) presents natural-rate shocks as representing supply shocks, such as those to productivity; a productivity shock would also move the natural rate and is not modelled here

cost_push_shock.shock: the cost-push term adds 1 percentage point a year to the Phillips curve on impact; inflation itself rises by more because firms expect the shock to last. The model has no energy sector; the cost-push term stands in for any rise in firms' costs

active.plain: The rate rises more than one for one with inflation, and the model has exactly one bounded path after any shock.

passive.plain: The rate rises less than one for one with inflation, and the model has many bounded paths, so the three equations alone do not say which one the economy follows.

rule_on.announcement: today (quarter 0) the central bank announces a one-quarter shift of 1 percentage point a year down in the intercept of its rule, in quarter 8 only; the rule stays on in every quarter; perfect foresight and rational expectations after the announcement

pegged_puzzle.announcement: the nominal policy rate is held at its steady-state value until the promised quarter, is 1 percentage point a year lower in that quarter only, then follows the rule
pegged_puzzle.reported_as: today's response for a cut promised h quarters ahead, divided by today's response to the same cut made today (h = 0)
pegged_puzzle.published_version: Del Negro, Giannoni and Patterson (2023), the version the committee's scientific background cites (p. 46)
pegged_puzzle.puzzle: in this textbook model, with the nominal rate held still until the promised quarter, the response today grows with how far ahead the promised cut is; Del Negro, Giannoni and Patterson (2012, 2015; published 2023) call this the forward guidance puzzle and McKay, Nakamura and Steinsson (2016) also find it implausible

a.question: An energy-price shock raises firms' costs. In this model, does the rule raise or lower the policy rate?
a.because: inflation goes up more than the output gap goes down, weighted by the rule

b.question: If the rate rises less than one for one with inflation (0.8), what happens in the model?
b.answer: no unique bounded solution: the model allows many paths, so it does not pin down what happens

c.question: A promise about the rate two years from now: does it move inflation today?
c.caveat: with the nominal rate held still until the promised quarter (pegged_puzzle) the effect today grows with the horizon: the forward guidance puzzle
